title: UGPU: Dynamically Constructing Unbalanced GPUs for Enhanced Resource Efficiency
problem: Physical GPUs maintain a fixed, balanced ratio of compute and memory resources, which is inefficient when co-executing workloads have heterogeneous compute-to-memory demands. Partitioning a GPU into unbalanced slices requires accurate performance prediction under variable resource allocations and causes heavy data migration overhead when memory resources are redistributed.
motivation: Cloud GPUs serving multiple concurrent tenants waste resources because no single balanced configuration is optimal for the diverse compute-memory ratios of simultaneously running applications.
method: UGPU dynamically divides a single GPU into unbalanced slices, each with a custom amount of compute resources (SMs, or Streaming Multiprocessors) and memory (HBM, or High Bandwidth Memory), using a demand-aware algorithm that figures out what workloads need without complex mathematical models. When rebalancing memory across slices, instead of using traditional slow page migration, UGPU introduces PageMove, which exploits the fact that all HBM memory channels already share physical TSV connections (vertical wires through the DRAM stack), allowing it to move pages in parallel across different bank groups simultaneously. PageMove pairs this parallel channel exploitation with a customized memory address mapping and Parallel Page Migration Mode (PPMM), achieving high-throughput page migration across memory dies without the latency cost.
key_novelty: PageMove uses the pre-existing vertical connections (TSVs) through the DRAM stack that link HBM memory channels to execute parallel page migrations simultaneously across memory bank groups, eliminating the latency overhead that blocks dynamic GPU slice reconfiguration.
contributions: First study of dynamically constructing unbalanced GPU slices from a single physical GPU for multi-tenant cloud workloads.
Demand-aware resource partitioning algorithm that adaptively sizes compute and memory slices without a performance model.
PageMove: a lightweight HBM architecture extension enabling parallel page migration across bank groups via TSV connections.
Custom memory address mapping and PPMM protocol integrated with virtual memory management to support live slice reconfiguration.

metrics.other: PageMove reduces page migration overhead vs. traditional migration (magnitude not stated in abstract)

limitations: Requires minor DRAM architecture modifications and a custom address mapping, potentially limiting applicability to existing HBM-equipped GPUs without hardware changes.
primary_theme: dynamic unbalanced GPU resource partitioning for multi-tenant efficiency
